transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Do not use the oven again until it has been checked by a qualified appliance engineer. A smell only when it is heating can be burnt food or grease, but an electrical or melting-plastic smell can indicate an overheating connection or heating-element fault, which is a fire risk. Once it is cold and isolated, you can look inside for obvious burnt-on spillages or packaging—do not remove panels or disturb wiring. Does the smell seem like hot food/grease from inside the cavity, or electrical burning/plastic from the controls, back or vents?
more like hot plastic or electrical I think, and it seems to come from behind or below the cooker, not inside the oven. the cooker switch on the wall looks a bit brown at one corner and felt warm too

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Do not use the cooker again until it has been checked by a qualified electrician or cooker engineer. Browning and warmth at the wall cooker switch, together with an electrical/plastic smell, strongly suggest an overheating connection or switch mechanism; that is a fire risk, rather than normal oven heat. The underlying cause could be the wall switch itself, its terminals/cable, or a fault in the cooker drawing excessive current, so both the switch and cooker supply need inspecting. Do not remove the switch cover or try tightening anything yourself.

candidates: Heating element or its connection overheating (medium)
Food or grease residue burning off (low)
